title: Student's t-Statistic under Unimodal Densities
one_line_what_it_does: Edgeworth/finite-sample analysis of t-intervals over symmetric unimodal laws; Sec. 2 remark: for symmetric +-1 Bernoulli, P(T_n=inf)=2^(1-n)>alpha when n<1-log(alpha)/log2, so no bounded t-based interval exists. A one-paragraph remark about t-intervals for one distribution; no theorem, no general procedures, no finite population.

title: Interval estimation of a median
venue_or_arxiv: Scand. J. Statist. 1:28-32 (as cited by Kuchibhotla et al.)
how_read: not read; via Remark 1 of arXiv:2403.06357
one_line_what_it_does: Locally bounded CI for median of symmetric laws impossible for n<log2(1/alpha) (Theorem 2 as claimed had log2(2/alpha); Kuchibhotla et al. say the claimed bound is false but proof gives log2(1/alpha)).

title: Inference for Median and a Generalization of HulC
how_read: Remark 1 and intro read in full text
one_line_what_it_does: Shift-invariant bounded median CI when n>=log2(2/alpha); conjectures none exists below log2(2/alpha) (= 1+log2(1/alpha), same threshold as 2^(1-n)>alpha).

title: Potscher & Preinerstorfer: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Size Controllability of Heteroskedasticity Robust Test Statistics
how_read: full text Sections 1-2 + start of appendix; keyword scan of rest
one_line_what_it_does: Gaussian heteroskedastic regression, single restriction: finite size-controlling critical value exists iff no hat-matrix-diagonal-1 row enters the restriction (Thm 2.2); else size=1 for every C; smallest control. critical value C(alpha)>=C*. Invariance under location-scale group G(M0) as in (E). No sampling/finite population/probability-graded threshold.

title: Valid Heteroskedasticity Robust Testing
one_line_what_it_does: General existence of smallest size-controlling critical values; sufficient condition (7), necessary (10).

title: Controlling the size of autocorrelation robust tests
one_line_what_it_does: General theory of size control via concentration phenomenon & invariance; basis of PP 2025.

title: Limitations of randomization tests in finite samples
how_read: Sections 1-4 (Props 1-7) in full; keyword scan of appendix
one_line_what_it_does: Necessary & sufficient condition for a null to admit a randomization test; mean-zero nulls admit none (iid, finite or continuous support). No confidence intervals, no finite population, no unbounded sets.

title: Some impossibility results for inference with cluster dependence with large clusters
how_read: abstract, intro, keyword scan of full text
one_line_what_it_does: Asymptotic: with one large cluster the mean cannot be consistently discriminated; long-run variance not consistently estimable.
bears_on_which_claim: context for cluster impossibility; no overlap with finite-sample max-share thresholds

title: Genuinely Robust Inference for Clustered Data
authors: H. Chiang; Y. Sasaki; Y. Wang
how_read: abstract, intro, Thm 1-2 statements, keyword scan
one_line_what_it_does: Asymptotic normality of cluster-robust t iff largest-cluster score is ignorable (a max-share-to-zero condition); otherwise stable limits; proposes cluster-score bootstrap. No finite-sample impossibility or equivariance class.
bears_on_which_claim: K(kappa0) class (asymptotic cousin of max-share); THEOREM2 (none)

title: Worst-case Nonparametric Bounds for the Student T-statistic
one_line_what_it_does: Maximises tail of Rademacher-weighted sums; k-sparse equal-weight maximisers. Pinelis comment (2509.02410) says main result incorrect/proof flawed.
bears_on_which_claim: none (sign-change distribution of T; no coverage-boundedness result)

title: Comment on 'Worst-case Nonparametric Bounds for the Student T-statistic'
one_line_what_it_does: Disputes Edelman's Theorem 1.

title: Robustness of standard confidence intervals for location parameters under departure from normality
one_line_what_it_does: Infimum coverage of t-interval over symmetric unimodal laws: attained at U[-1,1] for high levels, zero for t_{alpha/2}<1. Not an unboundedness/impossibility result over all procedures.

title: The nonexistence of 100(1-alpha)% confidence sets of finite expected diameter in errors-in-variables and related models
authors: L. J. Gleser; J. T. Hwang
one_line_what_it_does: Confidence sets with positive level must have infinite expected diameter when parameter is locally almost unidentified.

title: Some impossibility theorems in econometrics with applications to structural and dynamic models
one_line_what_it_does: Valid level 1-alpha sets for locally almost unidentified parameter must be unbounded with probability close to 1-alpha near non-identification; Wald sets have zero level.
bears_on_which_claim: LEMMA0; THEOREM1 (general principle; (2.7) of BM is the version)

title: Impossible inference in econometrics: theory and applications
how_read: Theorem 3 and Remark 4 read in text; rest scanned
one_line_what_it_does: Type A/B impossibility. Thm 3: if a common limit law P* is approached by models with unbounded parameter range then P*[D[C]=inf]>=1-alpha and C unbounded with positive probability nearby. Abstract general principle; needs continuity conditions; no finite population.
bears_on_which_claim: LEMMA0; THEOREM1 (general principle; not the finite-population graded form)

title: Finite Population Identification and Design-Based Sensitivity Analysis
one_line_what_it_does: Without assumptions on non-sampled units nothing can be said about the finite-population mean (identification statement); with bounds [0,1] gives identified set. Informal ancestor of Lemma 0's content; no coverage theorem.

title: Limiting distributions in simple random sampling from a finite population
venue_or_arxiv: Publ. Math. Inst. Hung. Acad. Sci. 5:361-374
one_line_what_it_does: Sample mean asymptotically normal iff max squared deviation / variance divided by min(n,N-n) -> 0 (Lindeberg-Hajek); in our notation kappa*G/min(n,G-n)->0.

title: General forms of finite population central limit theorems with applications to causal inference
how_read: statement of Thm 1 read in snippet
one_line_what_it_does: States Hajek condition and shows m_N/v_N >= 1-1/N.

title: Exact optimal confidence intervals for hypergeometric parameters
one_line_what_it_does: Exact CIs for hypergeometric M or N; Wald-type intervals have coverage as low as n/N. Bounded support [0,N] built in, so zero-event unboundedness does not arise.
bears_on_which_claim: (g) rare-unit coverage; not an overlap with THEOREM1/2

title: On non-parametric testing, the uniform behaviour of the t-test, and related problems
one_line_what_it_does: Bahadur-Savage-type: no bounded CI for the mean without restrictions; coverage zero if bounded for even one F.

title: Confidence sequences for sampling without replacement
one_line_what_it_does: Finite-sample CIs/CSs for SRSWOR under bounded support assumption.
bears_on_which_claim: THEOREM2 context (bounded-outcome route to finite-sample validity)

title: Dimension comparison for Student's statistic under symmetric unimodality
one_line_what_it_does: Edgeworth boundary / least favourability of uniform; about t-statistic under unimodality.
